html:
SMTO-LLM-0036 — A model setting wasn't accepted

GUID: 4fa407e2-4efd-49ea-b28a-8178f5734cf8
Slug: execution-parameter-rejected
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: provider

What happened

  • One of your model's settings has a value that SMTO or the model service won't accept, so the request didn't go through. Your saved settings weren't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Technical details in this panel and note which setting the message names. The message lists the exact setting that was refused, so you only change that one.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, open the Main card, and find that setting under Generation. Correct its value or switch it off, then select Save Main. A setting whose switch is off isn't sent, so the model service uses its own default value.
  3. Start a new task to use the corrected setting. A stopped task keeps the settings it started with, even when you resume it.

What success looks like

  • The Main card saves without warnings, and the new task's first model step runs without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO or your model service. Don't keep resubmitting with the same setting value; it will be refused again.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An execution request override failed local validation (unknown key, wrong type or value, invalid combination, or unknown profile mode), or the provider rejected a configured parameter that compatibility negotiation could not drop.

What this means

  • Execution overrides must satisfy local parameter schemas and cross-field limits as well as the provider's supported options; rejection can occur before transport. This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • Execution overrides must satisfy local parameter schemas and cross-field limits as well as the provider's supported options; rejection can occur before transport.

How to diagnose it

  • Check whether local validation or the provider rejected the setting; compare the named key, allowed range and output reservation without exposing private override contents.

How to fix it

  • Read rejected_execution_parameters or the validation message in the error details. In Settings › Setup › Model routing, edit that parameter in the role's Generation section: correct the value, or switch the parameter off so the provider default applies (or choose the Provider Defaults profile), then save. Existing tasks keep their captured settings on Resume, so start a new task to apply the change.
  • In Model Configuration, correct the rejected parameter or select Provider Default for a new task. Resume retains the saved execution settings.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A new task captures valid overrides and the provider accepts the intended request or omits that option under Provider Default.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
